title: Most people expect the test before the blessing.
paragraphs: Most people expect the test before the blessing.

Before the promise.
Before the breakthrough.
Before the miracle.
But Abraham’s story reveals something different.
God gave him the promise first.

After decades of waiting.
After years of believing.
After hoping when nothing seemed possible.
Finally, the impossible happened.
Isaac was born.

The child of promise.
The child Abraham prayed for.
The child that represented God’s faithfulness.
And then… something unexpected happened.
The test came later.

Not when Abraham had nothing.
Not when he was still waiting.
But when the promise was already in his hands.
God said something that must have felt impossible to hear:
“Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love… and offer him.” (Genesis 22)
Imagine the weight of that moment.

The son he waited decades for.
The miracle he prayed for.
The promise God Himself gave.
Now God was asking Abraham to trust Him with it.
This is where many people misunderstand faith.
Faith is not only trusting God to give something.
Faith is trusting God with what He already gave you.
Anyone can believe while waiting.
But true faith is revealed when the blessing finally arrives.

When the dream becomes real.
When the prayer is answered.
When the promise becomes something you can actually hold.
Because now there is something to lose.
That’s when the deeper question appears.
Do you trust God for the promise…
or do you trust Him with the promise?
Abraham walked up that mountain carrying more than wood for the altar.
He carried decades of hope.
He carried the future of the promise.
He carried the tension between love and obedience.
And yet, he still walked.
Step by step.
Not knowing what would happen.
But believing that God was still faithful.
And at the very moment the knife was raised…
God stopped him.
The test was never about Isaac.
It was about Abraham’s heart.
It was about trust.
And God provided the ram in the thicket — the sacrifice that would take Isaac’s place.
That moment became one of the most powerful truths in Scripture:

God is not trying to take your promise.
He’s testing your trust.
Sometimes the hardest tests don’t come when you're starting.
They come when you're established.

When life is finally stable.
When the blessing has finally arrived.
When the prayers you prayed years ago have finally been answered.
Because the real test is not always in the waiting.
Sometimes the real test is in the holding.
Will you still trust God when the promise is real?
Will you still obey when it costs something?
Will you still surrender the thing you love most?
Abraham’s story reminds us of something powerful:
God doesn’t test us to destroy us.
He tests us to reveal the depth of our faith.
And often, right when the tension feels unbearable…
God provides a way we never expected.
So if you're in a season where your faith is being stretched…
If you're holding something precious and feeling the tension of trust…
Remember Mount Moriah.
The place where obedience met provision.
The place where faith was proven.
And the place where God showed that He sees, He knows, and He provides.
Because sometimes…
The test comes late.
But so does the miracle.
📖 Genesis 22
